subject: BrightLane vendor comparison & packaging options
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightlane.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: BrightLane Procurement <procurement@brightlane.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLane RFP follow-up: pricing and packaging asks

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the private deployment options. Procurement asked me to get a compact comparison across economics and packaging because we're evaluating a vendor replacement for our inference stack. Key asks:

- Can Redwood provide a vendor-match proposal that shows equivalent/per-seat pricing and any onboarding credits?
- What packaging options exist for committed capacity vs. burstable usage?
- Are there any SKUs for long-term data retention and audit logs (we have strict compliance needs)?

I've attached the RFP and a short vendor checklist. We aim to have a recommendation by 9/6. Can you put together a short packet (1-2 pages) comparing pricing, the migration handoff, and recommended concessions?

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightLane

Attachments: BrightLane_RFP_2026.pdf
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightlane.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane RFP follow-up: pricing and packaging asks

Hi Elaine,

Appreciate the clarity — we'll put together a concise comparison and a recommended packaging option that balances your cost and uptime objectives. I'll share a draft with the procurement team and our internal pricing forum today. Expect a 2-page packet + spreadsheet by EOD PT.

Quick clarifying Qs to make sure our packet is aligned:
1) Migration timeline target: is 6-8 weeks post-contract signature acceptable?
2) Are there specific SLAs (p50/p95 latency targets) we should anchor to in the comparison?
3) Any constraints on data residency or third-party KMS?

I'll follow up with our proposal and a line-by-line econ sheet.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightLane RFP follow-up: pricing and packaging asks

Team — forwarding BrightLane's note. They want a vendor-match packet and explicit onboarding credits/packaging options. Draft deliverables: 1-2 page executive summary, a price comparison spreadsheet, and a recommended concession table (credits, trial capacity, SLA guardrails). Specific asks below.

Key constraints:
- Procurement target decision by 9/6.
- Likely negotiation leverage: migration assistance + one-time credits to cover egress/their downgrade risk.

Proposed approach:
- Option A (Commit): 12-month reserved pool, 20% discount vs list, 6-week onboarding credit (X GPU-hours).
- Option B (Burst + Reserve): smaller committed baseline + burst pool; lower upfront discount, include KV-caching configuration and 30-day performance credits.
- Technical warranty: 30-day rollout SLO with a rollback clause and code-level runbook handoff.

Connor — can you prepare the migration uplift estimate and a rough GPU-hours credit number? Marissa — please update the price spreadsheet and propose a compact concession ladder. Jordan — any runbook/legal caveats we should highlight?

I'll assemble into the single packet for BrightLane. Quick turnaround appreciated.

—Grace
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightLane RFP follow-up: pricing and packaging asks

Grace/Marissa —

Ran a quick estimate from the migration playbook + their stated volume. Rough numbers:
- Lift & shift (6 weeks): ~1,200 GPU-hours (training/validation + dry runs) — suggest offering 1,200 GPU-hours as onboarding credit for Option A.
- Expected steady-state monthly usage: ~35M tokens (inference) => we'd recommend Dedicated small pool (1-2 GPUs) with autoscale for peak.
- Migration risk buffer: offer a 2-month temporary burst credit bucket (equivalent to 800 GPU-hours) to ensure no throttling during ramp.

I'll attach a small spreadsheet with assumptions. If we offer both the 1,200 onboarding credit and 800 burst buffer, net present cost to Redwood is significant but should land us as the vendor-match leader.

-Connor

Attachments: redwood_price_comp_20260831.xlsx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightLane RFP follow-up: pricing and packaging asks

This looks good — a few pricing choices I recommend so we can tier concessions without killing ARR:

- SKU structure: keep three SKUs (dedicated, burst, retention add-on). Show list vs. committed discount ladder (10/15/20% at 6/12/24 month commits).
- Concession ladder: onboarding credit (1,200 GPU-hours) + 30% discount on first-month usage or a one-time migration credit of $45k — whichever they prefer.
- SLA credit: 5% service credit for missed monthly p95 targets; add a rollback clause for first 60 days.

I'll produce a short PDF exec summary (MAP_proposal_v2.pdf) that cadres these options and shows an apples-to-apples TCO column vs their incumbent.

-Marissa

Attachments: MAP_proposal_v2.pdf
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightlane.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane RFP follow-up: pricing and packaging asks

Hi Elaine — attaching the short packet and the support spreadsheet per your timeline. Highlights:

- Option A (12-month commit): 20% list discount, 1,200 GPU-hours onboarding credit, 800 GPU-hours burst buffer for two months.
- Option B (6-month commit + burst): 15% list discount, reduced onboarding credit (600 GPU-hours), includes audit-log retention add-on SKU at a fixed monthly price.
- Migration plan: 6-week kickoff, three phased milestones (pilot, lift, cutover), full runbook and smoke-test checklist included.
- SLA & rollback: 30-day performance guardrail with a 60-day rollback window; financial SLA credits (5% of monthly fee) if p95 exceedance persists.

Attachments: MAP_proposal_v2.pdf, redwood_price_comp_20260831.xlsx

If this aligns, Jordan can loop in Legal to codify the rollback and SLA terms. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
